analysis:
Examined workflow metadata, every patch hunk, and supplied BASE source through line 1052. .github/workflows/ci.yml HEAD lines 53–64 add macOS sandbox lanes; lines 232–234, 477–479, 675–677, 878–880, 1010–1012, 1072–1074 and 1134–1136 replace fixed runners with route outputs and add route dependencies. Lane counts match job predicates and shard names. Existing read-only token permissions, credential-free checkout, push-only cache writes, bounded execution and test-count audits are not changed. No direct change to runtime authorization, attestation, encryption, plaintext handling or billing is evidenced; T-041 cache mitigations remain untouched.
The new runner destination affects the execution environment for provider security/native tests and their reports, relevant to A-017, T-054 and TB-003/TB-007. Integration must examine .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml and its routing implementation: whether macOS destinations are trusted for test-result integrity, isolate untrusted PR execution from host credentials and other workloads, and reset between jobs. Also verify fallback/output completeness and reservation lifetime for test-provider-summary, which waits for all shards after routing. These contracts are outside the supplied evidence; adversarial provider ownership alone does not prove that CI runners lack isolation. No supported regression is established locally, but runner trust and lifecycle remain material unresolved questions. Later GPU/focused job bodies and the provider-ci-build action were not supplied.
